from the national synodal assembly in answer to the question, “what does god want of the church at this time?”, t he proposals suggest at first glance what god m ight be asking us to do. but there is something else! they are also pointing to what god might be asking us to be. or what god might be asking us to become. actions can too easily be put in a corner and be seen as the responsibility of someone else. but becoming is something that belongs to us all. it’s about our shared identity – not just about what we do, but who we are. it’s about growth. it’s about conversion. it’s about becoming the people that god wants us to be. actions can be decided, implemented, and completed. but growth, change, conversion, becoming – are a journey over time. a journey of becoming a church that proclaims the gospel a church that is a community of belonging a church that is a place of healing a church that accompanies a church that empowers for ministry and co-responsibility. the proposals now find their place in a vision of the church that we are seeking to become. and we can all find ourselves in this vision of the church. the pathways offer a real alternative to the polarised and polarising discourse that characterises so much of the life of our church and our w orld. they offer us a way of being together. and long after recommendations from today have been decided, implemented, evaluated, the p athways will continue to offer us ways of becoming, ways of finding our identity, and ways of walking the path together. fr. declan hurley , national synodal assembly , “hunger cannot be considered a statistical anomaly, for it is caused mainly by a lack of political will and collective charity. nor are food shortages geographically unavoidable. indeed, in an era of greater technological advancement than ever before, it is intolerable that bread should be considered a privilege and water a contested commodity. regular access to safe, adequate and sufïcient food, in keeping with the dignity of every person, is a basic human right. guaranteeing this right is an obligation of justice that binds both in dividual states and the internation- al community. and yet, while innovations accelerate production, distribution is being negle cted. grain markets are being optimized on stock exchanges, while the actual seeds that germinate in the soil fall into the hands of monopolies that suffocate small-scale farming. …. the myth that growth can be endless when resources are limited has reached breaking point. today, innovation requires adopting an intergenerational sense of responsibility that looks beyond annual budgets. innovation means re conciling technology with wisdom, including ancestral wisdom, while maintaining a vision for the future. it is not a matter of rejecting technological advances, but rather of integrating them with the wisdom o f farmers who have deepened their understanding of the soil and the climate through centuries of consc ientious observation. this likewise involves protecting water as an inalienable common good. ” pope leo’s message for the 2026 world food day november is the month we pray especially for our family, p (aps 21, 4). death is the prolongation, in a new way, of life as the liturgy says: "for your faithfu l, o lord, life has changed not ended; while our earthly dwelling is destroyed, a new and eternal come and �nd peace in the lord. also on the first saturday of every month- devotions in clara church at 2.55pm. everyone welcome to attend. join us for evena brief period of time. the commandments of love. in our gospel this week when jesus was asked which was the greatest commandment of the law of moses, he answered, not with his own words or ideas, but with the words of god to moses and with the words he himself, as a jewi shman, prayed twice each day. we hear them in the gospel as god’s word to us as christians. if we are being called in our present world to do one thing – then it has to be the call to proclaim love and hope in a world increasingly hearing calls to and fear. all around us, in midterm elections, in riots in european cities, in wars ravaging whole regions of our world, in tariff wars, in soaring gas and diesel prices, in rising inflation and cost of living, leaders and politicians and those with vested int erests in unrest and polarisation, sow seeds of hate and use fear as a we apon to divide people. never before has this gospel been more pertinent and relevant to our times. we live within a divided and fearful world, but we should not give our alleg iance to a divided and fearful world. our allegiance is to the kingdom of god; the kingdom won for us by jesus; the kingdom w here death is conquered by resurrection, hate is conquered by love, and fear is conquered by hope; the kingdom where we can “love the lord our god with all our heart, and with all our soul, and with all our mind… and love our neighbour as ourselves.” collections 17th/18th october – development fund: €960 ; mission sunday: €1,415 ; october offerings: €685 . thank you very much! increase worldwide as number of priests edges upward the number of catholics worldwide rose by 16.69 million to 1.422 billion last year. catholics accounted for 17.8 percent of a global population of almost 8 billion. for the first time in five years, there is an increase in the total number of priests in the world. the total reached 407,421, up 425 from the previous year. africa was the only continent to register an increase in religious sisters. the number of seminarians fell by 2,891 to 103,604. lay missionaries increased by 18,473 to 463,079. the church also runs 75,448 kindergartens, 103,666 primary schools, and 51,810 secondary schools. healthcare and charitable network include 101,110 facilities, 5,397 hospitals as well as 13,646 dispensaries. pope leo xiv's doctors confirm'no further treatment is necessary' pope leo xiv’s doctors confirm that the tumour removed earlier this month was a lung adenocarcinoma and that the disease was localised, noting that "no further treatment is necessary." we continue to keep the holy father in our prayers. first holy communion classes for children not attending catholic schools the classes begin in november on these dates: sunday 8 november, sunday 15 november, sunday 22 november, and sunday 29 november. the classes will take place in the family room (beside the altar) in the parish church immediately after 11am mass. young adults (18-30) faith group the next gathering will take place on monday 16 november at 7.30pm. parish pastoral council next meeting will take place on wednesday 4 november at 7pm. coeliacs for holy communion we now have the option for coeliacs to receive a low-gluten host for holy communion. these consecrated hosts will be kept in a separate pix for reception from the priest at the altar rails. trim active retirement group social thursday 29 october, castle arch, supper and music 5.30pm music. christmas party sunday 13 december castle arch hotel 1pm.

. the parish pastoral team held their recent monthly meeting. among the items discussed and planned were 1. harvest mass. 2. preparations for the masses of remembrance and for deceased children in november. 3. there was feedback from the recent meeting of the parishes from the pastoral area. 4. the parish baptism policy was again reaffirmed, with the members of the baptismal team thanked and acknowledged for their great work. it was noted that all baptism arrangements can only be made with the baptismal team at the monthly meeting in the parish centre, held on the first thursday of every month, and not through the parish office. 5. the recent blessing of pets to mark the end of the season of creation was noteworthy. 6. a mass of remembrance for the members of the local deceased sporting clubs was agreed for november 21st at 6 p.m.and the deceased religious and priests will have a special mass on november 22nd at 12 noon. 7. preparations were begun for the annual service in january to mark the week of prayer for christian unity. the parishes of the emmaus pastoral area held their autumn meeting last week. they shared ideas and suggestions on sacramental preparation in their parishes. there was a short discussion on youth development with offering the samuel group to young people and the upcoming youth day in mullingar on novemb er 22nd. they had presentations from the bethany team and a timely one on addiction from fasn. they have also agreed on an evening of retreat and recollection in the spring for our pastoral area.
